Internal helper: a bare word typed where a quoted value goes

Source: R/checks.R
dot-jst_word_args.Rd

Ruling R18 (Session 355; built Session 356): a variable is named without quotes, and anything that is not a variable – a format, a convention, a method, a level, a plot name – goes in quotes. A user who types jconvert(d, to = stata) or jplot(r, which = effects) meets R's own lookup of the word: "object 'stata' not found", or, when R finds a function of that name (effects, lm, mean), an error from deeper in that has nothing to do with the call. This check runs at the function's front door, before anything is evaluated, and stops with jload()'s form: the word, that it is not in quotes, and the call to run.

Usage

.jst_word_args(cl, mc, env, specs, fn)

Arguments

cl

The call as typed (sys.call()).

mc

The matched call (match.call(expand.dots = TRUE)).

env

The caller's environment, where a symbol is looked up.

specs

A named list, one entry per argument checked: a list with values (the accepted words, in the spelling the function takes), noun (what the argument takes, for the sentence: "a format name") and, optionally, name_it = TRUE; the shared entries come from .jst_word_specs().

fn

Character(1); the user-facing function's name, for the prefix.

Value

Invisible NULL; stops when a bare word is found.

Details

It fires on a bare symbol – or a c() of symbols and strings – that spells one of the argument's own values (compared without regard to case; the printed line spells the value as the function takes it) and does not evaluate to a character value. A name holding a value still works (fmt <- "stata"; to = fmt), and a word that is not one of the values is left to R and to the argument's own choice error, as before.

The line to run is the call as typed (sys.call()), with the one argument quoted: a named argument stays named, a positional one stays in its place unless its spec says name_it, for a function whose first position is read several ways (joptions(spss) is given as joptions(missing.convention = "spss")). The line is built on one line; the wrapper layer lays it out (ruling R5).
